A1.justification: The PDFs describe successive versions of the same token-filtering system, renamed from Collider to CENTRIFUGE. Both are readable, including equations, figures and tables. V1 has no appendix; v2's Appendices A-D were included in the comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original downstream-task results, training-time measurements, sensitivity experiments and an n-gram reference-model analysis, including Tables 2-3 and Figures 9 and 11-13.

after.justification: V2 reports original downstream-task results, convergence experiments and efficiency measurements across model sizes and training configurations in Tables 1-2 and Figures 4-5.

M1.justification: V1 Section 3.1 filters softmax activations, or Q/K activations for FlashAttention. V2 Section 4.1 introduces separate backward computations: key/value gradients use retained-token activations, while query gradients also incorporate discarded-token key/value contributions. This substantively changes gradient computation to avoid interference. The dimension-reduced GEMM and automatic graph-update mechanisms are retained.

E1.justification: Both retain OpenWebMath mathematical adaptation and the same nine downstream benchmarks, including GSM8K, MATH and MAWPS. No additional dataset, domain or downstream task is reported. Larger models, alternate reference models, tensor parallelism and LoRA change configurations within the retained coverage.

E2.justification: RHO, renamed loss-only filtering, is removed from the downstream accuracy and timing tables and the context-length comparison. It remains in v2's new convergence comparisons, which also introduce a naive activation-filtering strawman in Figure 4(a). The filtering-ratio comparison switches its reference from RHO to regular training, substantially revising the principal comparisons.

E3.justification: Main comparisons change from 40% to 50% token filtering. V2 drops Phi-1.5 and adds configurations up to 40B parameters, four-GPU data parallelism, tensor parallelism and single-GPU LoRA. Timing changes from a 512-sample iteration to processing one million tokens; Qwen2.5-1.5B context changes from 3K to 2K. The largest models use an additional H20/NVLink testbed.

E4.justification: V2 Figure 4 adds convergence tests under two reference-model choices and tests whether naive activation filtering causes failure. V1's n-gram versus transformer correlation/token-overlap analysis and operator-overhead sensitivity plot are removed. Context-length and filtering-ratio analyses remain but are revised, including different model configurations and a filtering-ratio sweep ending at 60% instead of 70%.

E5.justification: Both average efficiency measurements over ten iterations. Neither reports independent training-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bands. V2's newly stated warmup procedure does not change uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V1 Table 2's 40%-filtering result, averaging 20.7, is replaced by v2 Table 1's 50%-filtering result averaging 27.3; the regular-training average remains 17.8. V2 adds convergence findings and system results reaching 49.9% backward and 34.7% total time reductions. Old timing entries, full-training day estimates and n-gram results disappear. Changed methods and settings prevent interpreting these as matched-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 Section 4.1 replaces v1's shared activation-filtering rationale with distinct sparsity arguments for query versus key/value gradients. Equations 3-4 partition retained and discarded activations and derive their separate gradient contributions. This substantially revises the mathematical justification underlying the method; the token-selection objective remains unchanged.

C1.justification: V1 acknowledges lower utility than RHO and suggests further tuning. V2 asserts full preservation of loss-only filtering's utility and presents a specialized attention backward kernel as an explicit algorithmic contribution. Its headline efficiency claims also concern 50% filtering and models up to 40B, replacing the earlier small-model, 40%-filtering claims.

C2.justification: V1's explanation of utility loss through reduced gradients and unsuitable hyperparameters is removed. V2 explains strawman non-convergence through damaged query gradients, discusses model-size-dependent graph-update overhead, and introduces MoE load-balancing and long-context forward-filtering considerations. The reference-model cost caveat and compression/n-gram discussion disappear; most distributed-communication reasoning survives in Appendix D.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-hosting statement, identifies FlashAttention plus a cuDNN attention-bias kernel, and documents LoRA rank 64/projections, updated software and H20 hardware. It newly specifies two warmup iterations but omits v1's explicit 15B-token, one-epoch training budget. Most graph-generation code and integration instructions are retained in Appendices B-C rather than newly supplied.

R1.justification: V2 Section 2.2 substantially expands data-selection and parameter-efficient training coverage, adding works such as DoReMi, QuRating, RegMix, QLoRA and Compacter. It emphasizes model-adaptive token selection and complementarity with parameter-efficient methods, whereas v1 mainly describes parameter reduction as an alternative that may harm utility. Several earlier freezing/pruning references are removed.

P1.justification: Beyond the title and system rename, v2 extensively rewrites the motivation and attention explanation, separates observations from preliminary material, moves related work forward and places discussion after evaluation. Much of v1's graph-update, implementation and communication discussion moves into Appendices B-D, substantially reorganizing the narrative.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from two columns to one, combines v1 Figures 3-4 into Figure 2, adds convergence plots and redesigns the efficiency plots. Result tables change comparator rows and columns, including removal of the full-training-time column. Several illustrations and analysis plots disappear, while graph attributes, implementation diagrams and code listings move to appendices.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses an important weakness in v1's activation-filtering procedure with an explicit split-gradient kernel and targeted convergence evidence, rather than leaving utility loss to future tuning. Actual tensor-parallel, LoRA and large-model measurements substantially strengthen practical validation. Removing the direct RHO downstream comparison and reference-model cost discussion weakens support for complete utility preservation and total-cost claims, but these reporting losses do not outweigh the gains in the central method and its validation.
